HAPPY 24TH BIRTHDAY, INVINCIBLE (released on October 29, 2001)!

The Invincible album and its era were infamously overshadowed by a public dispute between Michael Jackson and his record label, Sony. After enduring the physically grueling HIStory tour, where he had to perform even while suffering from severe laryngitis and other health complications, Michael decided he would not tour again for this album.

Following six years of meticulous work and repeated delays, Invincible was finally completed. However, Sony was reportedly underwhelmed by the final product. The label believed that a world tour was essential to recoup their investment, as they lacked confidence in the commercial potential of the seven singles Michael had personally chosen. These were: Unbreakable (intended as the lead single with a cinematic short film), You Rock My World, Cry, Butterflies, Speechless, Whatever Happens, and Break of Dawn. Speechless was released as a promotional single only, while Break of Dawn was later included on the Number Ones compilation album two years afterward. Michael also mentioned to Elizabeth Taylor during a phone conversation that he had plans for Threatened, possibly another short film.

Ultimately, only You Rock My World and Cry received anything close to a proper release. All planned photo sessions for the album were cancelled, and much of the promotional budget was cut. This is why the single covers ended up being simple crops of the album artwork.

I’ve done my best to restore some of this album’s lost dignity by creating some custom single covers that reflect the care and artistry Michael originally intended. Of course, you’re free to revert to the original versions if you prefer, but I wanted to share the reasoning behind these changes. You’ll also find that several of the unreleased single choices appear as B-sides on the custom releases.

A commercial single was planned for release on January 15, 2002, but it was ultimately cancelled. After Sony refused to support the earlier singles and even appeared to sabotage them, Michael planned to relaunch the campaign with a self-financed single and short film for Unbreakable. For unknown reasons, he never followed through with these plans, and the single release scheduled for February 4, 2002, was ultimately cancelled. I chose to include Whatever Happens as the B-side to highlight another potential single that never came to fruition.
